scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9058: Hello, I'm on PC0 (20.1.1.x). I can't get through to
PC12 (120.1.1.x) on the far side of the network any more -- it times out
every time. I vaguely remember hearing our two sides run on "different
routing" somehow, but I honestly don't know what that means. Could someone
take a look at whatever connects the two sides and fix it? Thanks a lot!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The OSPF core is converged, R11 redistributes
  between OSPF and EIGRP, and PC0 (20.1.1.x) reaches PC12 (120.1.1.x) with 0% loss
  in both directions. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a redistribution / interior-link fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC0 cannot reach PC12
across the OSPF/EIGRP core -- is NOT reproducible: the OSPF backbone is converged,
R11 redistributes OSPF<->EIGRP (so the 120.x/EIGRP prefixes appear in the OSPF
RIB and vice versa), and PC0 reaches PC12 (120.1.1.x) with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: cross-core reachability is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the PC0->PC12
path, finds it working, optionally confirms R11's redistribution and the EIGRP
neighbors are up, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a broken
redistribution or a down interior link to satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The topology is a dual-routing-protocol design: the main backbone (r1–r10) runs OSPF in multiple areas, while the far-side cluster (r11–r12–r13) runs EIGRP AS 100. Router r11 is the boundary device, with one interface in OSPF area 0.0.0.3 (facing r1 via the 111.x.x.x segment) and two interfaces in EIGRP (facing r12 via 112.x.x.x and r13 via 103.x.x.x). This is exactly the "different routing on each side" the user vaguely recalled.

The redistribution at r11 is correctly configured: r11's OSPF process carries `redistribute eigrp` and `redistribute connected`, causing r1 to learn 120.0.0.0/8 (pc12's subnet) as an OSPF external route via r11 at 111.1.1.2. Confirmed via r1's FIB and the OSPF LSDB (r11 is advertising the 120.0.0.0 external LSA). On the reverse path, r12 carries a persistent kernel-static default route `0.0.0.0/0 via 112.1.1.1`, so pc12 reaches pc0 through r11 into the OSPF domain. EIGRP adjacencies on r11↔r12 and r11↔r13 have been stable since lab startup (~4.5 minutes), with no flap observed.

A Phase A–B–D sweep found no L2 anomaly, no traffic-control shaping, no resource pressure, and no service-layer fault. A concrete OSPF area-0.0.0.2 orphan was detected on r8, but r8 sits entirely outside the pc0→pc12 forwarding path (r8 is in the area 0.0.0.1 sub-domain; r1 routes to pc12 via r11 in area 0.0.0.3). End-to-end reachability is confirmed at 0% loss, 1.56 ms RTT.

Root cause: No anomaly is present. The user's reported timeouts are unconfirmed — there is no mechanism, historical trace, or flap process that would explain them, and the current network state is fully healthy.

Fix: No corrective action is required. Verify from pc0 that direct pings to 120.1.1.10 succeed; if the user still experiences issues, investigate the application layer or client-side configuration on pc0 rather than the network path.
